title: Edgewright
pitch: A redirect console a human and an agent drive together, over WebMCP. Test, audit and fix routing across 11 hosts, then prove a migration never breaks a link.
about_excerpt: A redirect console a human and an agent drive together, over WebMCP. Test, audit and fix routing across 11 hosts, then prove a migration never breaks a link. Like Comment Story Updates Edgewright turns your redirect and rewrite rules into a live console a human and an AI agent work together, over WebMCP. Test any URL, catch the rule that shadows another, translate a config to another host, then prove nothing breaks, all in the browser. The problem: redirect rules are ordered and first-match-wins. A broad rule above a specific one makes the specific one dead code, so a link works locally then 404s in production. Edgewright makes that visible and fixable, by a person or by an agent on the same page. How the tools are used: the console registers fifteen tools with document.modelContext.registerTool. In the demo the agent runs test_url to find the 404, audit_rules to name the shadowed rule, reorder_rule to fix the order, then test_url again. Read-only tools carry readOnlyHint so the agent runs them without a prompt. The tools that change rules omit it, so the agent asks first. The UI and the tools mutate one shared store, so a human clicking a button and an agent calling a tool run the exact same code. The product is three apps on one engine: the Console, Preflight (a pre-deploy gate), and Studio (migrate a config between hosts and prove every URL still resolves). Live: https://edgewright.vercel.app Source: https://github.com/zkasuran/edgewright Video: https://youtu.be/8Hry7ozQTe8 Built for the OpenAI WebMCP Challenge. The engine, @edgewright/core, covers eleven hosting platforms grounded in their own docs, with 148 passing tests, no build and no dependencies. For platforms whose routing is code, like Fastly and CloudFront, the engine resolves the trivial static patterns and labels the rest as not-simulated rather than guessing. Everything shown in the demo is the deployed product on the live URL or a real source file. The narration is synthesised speech. The design, the code, the review and the verification are the author's.
